items.name: directriz01
items.text:
WHAT TO PRESERVE AT ALL COSTS

-The opening hook — it must remain intact or nearly intact. It's the reason the viewer stays.
-Any scene or character that embodies the central thesis (in this script: the woman in the fleece vest at the city council). These are the moments that make the argument human. Never cut them.
-Concrete numbers and data. They are what separates argument from opinion.
-The cadence and sentence rhythm of the original. Short punching sentences followed by longer explanatory ones. This is the voice.
-The emotional arc: confusion → recognition → clarity. Every section must serve one of these three stages.

WHAT TO CUT FIRST

-Repeated ideas across different sections. Identify the single best version of each argument and cut the others entirely. Do not summarize the cut versions — delete them.
-Any paragraph that makes the same point as the previous one but with different words.
-Closing paragraphs that restate what the section already proved. Trust the reader.
-Transitional throat-clearing: phrases like "So let's talk about..." or "Here's the thing..." that delay the actual content.

STRUCTURAL APPROACH

-Read the full script and identify the 3 to 4 non-negotiable ideas. Everything else is supporting material that can be compressed or cut.
-For each section, ask: what is the single image or moment that carries this section's argument? Keep that. Cut everything around it that doesn't add new information.
-If two sections make similar arguments, merge them into one. Do not keep both.
-The closing should be half the length of any other section. Its job is emotional resolution, not new information.

WHAT NEVER TO DO

-Do not change the point of view or the "you" address. The intimacy is structural.
-Do not soften the argument to make it more palatable. The edge is the point.
-Do not add new content or examples not present in the original.
-Do not write transitions that explain what just happened. Cut and move forward.

FORMAT / B-ROLL (mandatory):
- Remove every [B-ROLL: …] tag from the SCRIPT section—standalone lines and inline. Do not add new ones.
- Do not describe shots in bracket tags; fold any essential visual detail into the spoken narration in plain prose.
- Keep [CATEGORIA: …] section headers and the OUTLINE structure.
- This project uses static AI images; B-roll tags are not read aloud and are handled downstream by routers—not in the script.
